overview:
The Retail Caucus is a consumer-goods megacorp bloc whose logistics hubs, warehousing monopolies, and shipping manifests quietly sustained Separatist supply lines throughout the Clone Wars. Led by Aqualish executive Po Nudo, the Caucus translated retail dominance into wartime quartermaster power — moving rations, spare parts, and droid components under civilian packaging codes.

Republic analysts often underestimated the Caucus because its HoloNet presence focused on marketplaces rather than battlefields, yet front-line Separatist armies depended on Caucus routing tables to keep foundries fed.
history:
Retail Caucus members built fortunes by controlling last-mile distribution on congested Core trade lanes, then leveraged that leverage to extract manufacturing concessions from supplier worlds. Po Nudo's Aqualish syndicate ties linked the Caucus to broader Rim networks beyond polite corporate branding.

When Po Nudo joined the Separatist Council, Caucus freighters gained CIS naval escorts while maintaining Republic retail licenses on paper. [Senator Onaconda Farr](characters/onaconda-farr) and [Padmé Amidala](characters/padme-amidala) investigated supply shortages that traced back to Caucus hoarding on Rodia and nearby sectors.

[General Grievous](characters/general-grievous) coordinated with Caucus quartermasters to prioritize droid foundry deliveries over civilian relief — a strategy that starved loyalist worlds while keeping Separatist factories at capacity. Jedi raids on Caucus warehouses rarely made headlines but materially shortened siege timelines.

Imperial post-war audits seized Caucus manifests as evidence of systemic profiteering, yet many subsidiary brands survived under new corporate shells.

**Key figures and documented associations.** Archives tie Retail Caucus operations to [Onaconda Farr](characters/onaconda-farr), [Padmé Amidala](characters/padme-amidala), [General Grievous](characters/general-grievous). Testimony from captains, senators, and hunter guild boards repeatedly name these individuals when reconstructing supply routes, succession disputes, and covert payroll networks — even when official holonews omitted the organization's role.

Intelligence annexes recommend cross-referencing their personal profiles when investigating Retail Caucus contracts, as individual loyalties often explain faction shifts that corporate ledgers alone cannot clarify.

**Territory and headquarters.** Primary operational worlds include Ando, Coruscant. Local customs officials, shadow-port syndics, and planetary governors maintained uneasy coexistence with Retail Caucus agents — taxing, bribing, or outsourcing enforcement depending on which side held the garrison that season.
significance:
The Retail Caucus illustrates how logistics monopolies can wage war by allocation rather than artillery. Its story complements better-known Separatist militaries with a supply-chain perspective historians now treat as decisive.

Caucus archives inform modern sanctions doctrine against dual-use consumer shipping.

**Documented across galactic media.** Retail Caucus appears in canonical records tied to Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones; Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith; Star Wars: The Clone Wars; Star Wars: The Bad Batch. Each appearance reinforces how the organization intersects with major wars, underworld economies, and Force-era purges — not as background color but as decision-making institutions with payrolls, territory, and succession law.
